title: Cognitive biases in adolescents with anorexia nervosa - an experimental study on mechanisms maintaining psychopathology
summary: Anorexia nervosa is a severe mental disorder that primarily affects adolescent and young women. Individuals with anorexia nervosa often show body image disturbances and tend to interpret information related to their body weight and shape negatively - they show so-called “cognitive biases”. It is assumed that these negative cognitive biases contribute to the ecaxerbation and maintenance of the disorder. The aim of this research project is to investigate this hypothesized relationship experimentally: we examine whether negative cognitive biases in adolescents with anorexia nervosa can be changed with the help of a special computerized training (so-called “CBM-I-training”) and whether this also improves eating disorder symptoms. The results will help us to better understand what role negative cognitive biases play in the maintenance of anorexia nervosa in adolescence - and whether they could be a possible starting point for new forms of treatment.

interventions.name:
CBM-I training:
A CBM-I training will be used to modify interpretation biases. CBM-I paradigms attempt to reduce negative interpretation biases by promoting benign (i.e. positive, self-serving or non-biased) interpretations of ambiguous information (Bradatsch et al., 2020; Koster et al., 2009; Math

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Diagnosis of anorexia nervosa or atypical anorexia nervosa according to DSM-5 criteria
- At the time of testing, the BMI must correspond to at least the 3rd age-corrected percentile
Exclusion criteria:
- below-average intelligence (IQ < 80)
- insufficient German language skills 
- psychotic disorders
- bipolar disorders
- Substance dependence (except tobacco/nicotine)
